evidence.quote: The user’s question is converted to embeddings using an embedding model such as “text-embedding-ada-002.” In the retrieval stage, the embeddings pertaining to the user query are used for a vector search in MongoDB Atlas to get similar chunks from the MongoDB Atlas collection.
In the Augmented stage, these chunks retrieved from MongoDB Atlas are added to the actual user query as context to create a prompt for the LLM.
MongoDB Atlas stores vector data alongside operational data without any additional overhead
Next, we will use Azure’s OpenAI service and its text-embedding-ada-002 model, which specializes in creating embeddings from text input.
Here’s how we generated embeddings for the book dataset using text-embedding-ada-002:

edits.rationale: The MongoDB blog establishes query embedding by an embedding model such as text-embedding-ada-002, Atlas vector search returning similar chunks, and those chunks being added as context for the LLM. A Synatic engineering post, a third-party source, shows Azure OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 generating embeddings for the documents that are then stored in MongoDB. Together these cover the whole claim. The MongoDB blog alone does not say Azure OpenAI embeds the documents.

edits.old: A framework integration can compose Spring AI’s MongoDBAtlasVectorStore, which accepts an EmbeddingModel, with its AzureOpenAiEmbeddingModel implementation. This is an application-managed alternative to the legacy managed connector, inferred from the two documented interfaces. (medium confidence)
edits.new: Spring AI’s MongoDBAtlasVectorStore takes an EmbeddingModel (any implementation), and in the Spring AI 1.1.x line AzureOpenAiEmbeddingModel is an EmbeddingModel implementation (via AbstractEmbeddingModel), so the two can be composed as an application-managed approach. As of Spring AI 2.0.0-M5, the docs say to use the OpenAI embeddings support to access OpenAI models deployed on Azure / Microsoft Foundry instead. Sources: https://docs.spring.io/spring-ai/reference/api/vectordbs/mongodb.html ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/1.1.x/models/spring-ai-azure-openai/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/azure/openai/AzureOpenAiEmbeddingModel.java ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/1.1.x/spring-ai-model/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/embedding/AbstractEmbeddingModel.java ; https://docs.spring.io/spring-ai/reference/api/embeddings/azure-openai-embeddings.html

edits.rationale: The Spring AI MongoDB page shows MongoDBAtlasVectorStore.builder(mongoTemplate, embeddingModel) and says the model can be any EmbeddingModel implementation. In the 1.1.x source, AzureOpenAiEmbeddingModel extends AbstractEmbeddingModel, which implements EmbeddingModel, so the pairing holds there. The current 2.0.x docs redirect Azure-hosted OpenAI embedding use to the OpenAI embeddings support, so the claim is version-dependent. The claim's own words call this an inference, and the sources support it. The comparison with the legacy managed connector was not checked.
